title: Standardize interactive states and responsive spacing across component libraries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Audit and remediate component variants so interactive states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled) follow a single naming convention and consistent layer order. Clean up auto-layout constraints to enforce responsive spacing token usage (spacing-sm/med/lg) and remove ad-hoc pixel offsets that break at 320–1440px widths. Goal: reduce developer confusion, prevent regressions during publish, and improve keyboard/focus visibility for high-contrast settings.
acceptance_criteria: All primary button, secondary button, table row, and chart controls expose consistent variant names: default / hover / pressed / focus / disabled.
Interactive state layers are ordered consistently (background -> icon -> label -> focus-ring) and use semantic token fills (semantic-bg, semantic-text, focus-ring-color).
Auto-layout frames use spacing token aliases (spacing-xxs..spacing-xl) rather than hard-coded pixel gaps, verified across a 320px, 768px, and 1366px artboard.
Publish checklist created and run for library publish containing visual diff review, keyboard focus QA, and a migration note for engineers.
Migration PR (tokens + layer renames) created with a clear changelog and linked GH changes for sync rollout.
No regressions reported in follow-up QA run; any regressions have triage notes and remediation steps.
Design console doc updated with new naming conventions and example snippets for component consumption.
tasks: Run full library audit script to detect non-standard variant names and ad-hoc spacing layers (script located in Confluence > Design Ops).
Create mapping table for current variant names -> canonical names, and publish mapping to the team for review.
Refactor 30 highest-traffic components (primary/secondary buttons, input, select, table rows, modal headers, small charts) to match canonical variant ordering and tokens.
Coordinate with engineering: add a temporary runtime alias layer for tokens to avoid immediate breaking changes (ENG-2410).
Update Figma library publish checklist entry and run first canary publish to 'internal-preview' team for visual diff pass.
Document migration notes for engineers including CSS token names and expected DOM changes.
Schedule 1-hour QA session with PM and 2 engineers to validate keyboard navigation and visual diffs.
Tag release in Design repo and notify SDK/Docs owners for downstream updates.

notes: Trade-offs: keeping runtime aliases increases short-term complexity for engineering but prevents breaking production. Longer-term plan is to fully migrate tokens in a single release window after feature-flagged rollout. QA should prioritize pages with highest active user counts (dashboard, create-task flow).
